title: Covariance Estimation Without Logarithmic Oversampling
statement: Let $X$ be a mean-zero random vector in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with covariance matrix $\Sigma$, and let $\Sigma_N$ be the empirical covariance matrix from $N$ independent samples. Characterize the distributions for which $\mathbb{E}\|\Sigma_N-\Sigma\|\leq\varepsilon\|\Sigma\|$ holds with $N=O(n)$. In particular, is linear sample size sufficient for every distribution having $2+\varepsilon$ moments?

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-21)

**Status:** partially solved

**Assessment.** Srivastava--Vershynin obtain N=O(n) under uniform 2+epsilon marginal regularity, resolving an important regime but not the unrestricted almost-never conjecture.
